security.title: Security and keys

point.password: The password stays on the device. The browser derives a key from it; only proof that you know it goes to the service.
point.browser: Data is encrypted in the browser. Names, titles, messages and answers reach the service already encrypted.
point.access: Access is a key. Whoever has an area's key reads its data; granting access passes on the key, revoking replaces it with a new one.
point.link: A link is a key too. A person with a link sees only what the link leads to — and only until you revoke it.
point.lost: The password cannot be recovered. Without it nobody, not even an administrator, can open your keys.

security.noDevices: The key is not kept anywhere.
security.forgetHint: A forgotten device is not signed out — it will ask for the password the next time it opens.

json.usageTitle: How the app uses this data
json.usage:
- The details lie with the person's role, each field separately, sealed with its key: only whoever has this person's key opens them (usually only you). The service only knows which fields are filled in.
- First and last name (or, without them, the nickname) are the person's name in the app: your roles and lists call them that, and the messages you send in conversations are signed that way.
- An area gets a field only when you share it (“My details”): the copy is sealed with the area's key and anyone with access to the area reads it — e.g. the area's list of people takes the first and last name from it.
- A form filled in for this person fills in the answers to questions about first name, last name, phone, date of birth, address, e-mail and nickname by itself. The import doesn't change submissions already sent.
- A share is withdrawn in “My details” (“Who got it”): the area loses the copy, but what someone has already read can't be undone.
json.title: My details as JSON ("{format}", version {version})
json.text:
Details of the persons this account runs: first name, last name, phone, date of birth, address, e-mail, nickname (Account, #/workspace/account → under “My details” → “My details as JSON”). Each field is sealed in the browser separately — with the person's key — and shared separately.
What the import does:
- First it shows a plan of changes; it saves only after “Import”.
- It changes only fields of this account's persons, named by "id" from the export. Persons without "id" or with someone else's "id" are skipped (warning) — it creates no persons or accounts and never changes someone else's details.
- A field with a new value is saved; the same value — no change. A change also refreshes the copies in areas this field was already shared with (the plan lists them); it shares nothing with new areas.
- Empty text ("") and null don't delete: the field stays as it was (it is deleted in “My details”, together with its shares).
- A value in the wrong shape (e.g. date, e-mail, phone) — warning, field skipped.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.
